items.q: List three privileges enjoyed by the First and Second Estates before the Revolution.

items.q: Explain how the Constitution of 1791 limited the powers of the King.
items.proposedAnswer: The Constitution of 1791 made France a constitutional monarchy. Powers were divided among the National Assembly, which made laws, the executive and the judiciary, so the King no longer held all power himself.

items.proposedAnswer: Peace meant ending Russia's part in the First World War, land meant transferring land to the peasants, and bread meant ending food shortages in the cities.

items.q: Why was the rule of the Tsar unpopular in Russia in the early twentieth century?
items.proposedAnswer: The Tsar ruled as an autocrat and did not share real power with the Duma, which he dismissed repeatedly. Workers and peasants lived in poverty, and military defeats in war added to the anger.

items.q: Explain how the Treaty of Versailles helped Hitler to gain support.
items.proposedAnswer: Many Germans felt humiliated by the war guilt clause, heavy reparations, loss of territory and limits on the army. Hitler promised to undo the treaty and restore German pride, which attracted support.

items.q: Give three reasons why rivers are important to the economy of a country.
items.proposedAnswer: Rivers provide water for irrigation and drinking, can be used to generate hydroelectricity, serve as waterways for transport, and deposit fertile soil along their banks.

items.q: Name any two measures taken in India to protect wildlife.

items.q: Explain why India has a rich variety of plants and animals.
items.proposedAnswer: India has varied relief, soils and climates, from rainy forests and wet coasts to deserts and snowy mountains. These different conditions allow many different kinds of plants and animals to live in the country.

items.q: How does the age composition of a population affect a country's economy?
items.proposedAnswer: A large working-age group can raise production and incomes, while many children and old people depend on workers and need spending on schools and care. The balance between workers and dependents shapes the economy.

items.q: State any two arguments in favour of democracy.
items.proposedAnswer: Democracy makes the government accountable to citizens, improves the quality of decisions through discussion, gives dignity and equality to citizens, and allows mistakes to be corrected.

items.q: Why is a democratic government considered more accountable than a dictatorship?
items.proposedAnswer: In a democracy rulers must face regular elections and can be removed by voters, and they must follow rules and answer to people and institutions. A dictator does not face such checks.

items.proposedAnswer: The legislature, such as Parliament, makes laws and controls the government, while the executive, such as the Prime Minister, Council of Ministers and civil servants, carries out and enforces those laws.

items.q: Why is an independent judiciary important in a democracy?
items.proposedAnswer: An independent judiciary can protect citizens' rights, settle disputes fairly and check whether laws and actions of the government follow the Constitution, without pressure from the government.

items.q: Why did the National Assembly abolish feudal obligations in August 1789?

items.q: Why is it not enough for a democracy to hold elections? Mention two other conditions.

items.q: What is the minimum support price?
items.proposedAnswer: The minimum support price is a price announced by the government at which it will buy certain crops from farmers, such as wheat and rice. It protects farmers from very low market prices.
keyPoints: Government buys crops at this price

items.q: How does the Public Distribution System help poor families when market prices rise?
items.proposedAnswer: Ration shops sell grain and other items at fixed, lower prices, so poor families are less affected by market price rises. The buffer stock held by the government helps to keep these supplies available.
keyPoints: Fixed lower prices at ration shops

items.q: Which colours make up the French tricolour flag?
Which words formed the motto of the French Revolution?
Which queen of France, the wife of Louis XVI, was executed in 1793?
Where was the royal court of Louis XVI based?
How did economic problems help to bring about the French Revolution?
options: Taxes were abolished for the Third Estate
Wars and royal spending emptied the treasury, bad harvests raised bread prices and heavy taxes burdened the Third Estate

items.q: What was the Tennis Court Oath?
items.proposedAnswer: In June 1789 members of the Third Estate, who had declared themselves the National Assembly, gathered in an indoor tennis court at Versailles. They swore not to separate until they had drafted a constitution for France.
keyPoints: Gathered at an indoor tennis court in Versailles

items.q: Explain how the ideas of the French Revolution spread beyond France.
items.proposedAnswer: Napoleon's armies and his Civil Code carried ideas such as equality before the law and the end of feudal privileges to other parts of Europe. The ideals of liberty and equality also inspired movements for rights and freedom elsewhere, including in colonies.
keyPoints: Ideas of liberty and equality spread

items.q: What is rule by one person with unlimited power called?

What happened to the land of nobles and the Church after the Bolsheviks took power?
options: It was returned to the Tsar
It was sold to foreign companies
It was taken over and given to peasants

items.q: Why did socialists such as Robert Owen set up cooperative communities?
options: To show people could live and work cooperatively and share property instead of competing for profit

items.q: Name two political groups that opposed the Tsar's rule in Russia.
items.proposedAnswer: Opposition groups included the Bolsheviks and Mensheviks, who were socialists, the Socialist Revolutionaries, who represented peasants, and liberals who wanted a constitution.

items.q: Marx expected revolutions in industrial countries, yet Russia, a mainly agricultural country, had one first. Give two reasons.
items.proposedAnswer: The Tsar's autocracy was weak and unpopular, and military defeats in the First World War worsened shortages and anger. Peasants wanted land, and workers in the big factories of cities were organised and ready to strike.
keyPoints: Defeats and shortages in the war

items.q: What title did Hitler take as the supreme leader of Nazi Germany?
By what name is Hitler's regime in Germany from 1933 to 1945 also known?
What was the Munich Putsch of 1923?
options: A failed attempt by Hitler to seize power in Bavaria
A victory parade of the army
An election won by the Nazis

items.q: What role did the Nazis expect women to play in society?
options: Mothers and homemakers who raised children, with fewer career opportunities

items.q: How did German rearmament in the 1930s affect the economy?
options: It created jobs through arms and public works, but also made war more likely

items.q: Why is Nazi Germany described as a totalitarian state?
options: It allowed full freedom of the press
It tried to control every part of life, including politics, media, education and culture
It left people free to decide their beliefs

items.q: What does the word propaganda mean?
items.proposedAnswer: Propaganda is the spreading of information, ideas or slogans, often one-sided or misleading, to influence what people think and to win support for a cause.

items.q: Describe how the Nazis dealt with political opponents after 1933.
items.proposedAnswer: The Nazis banned other political parties and trade unions, censored the press, and used the Gestapo to arrest opponents. Many were sent to concentration camps, which created fear and silenced opposition.
keyPoints: Arrests by the Gestapo and camps

items.q: Why are large deltas found along the east coast of India?
options: Large east-flowing rivers deposit silt at their mouths in the Bay of Bengal
The east coast has no rivers
The coast is covered with ice

items.q: Name any four physiographic divisions of India.
items.proposedAnswer: The main divisions are the Himalayan Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.

items.q: How do the Himalayas differ from the Peninsular Plateau in age and formation?
items.proposedAnswer: The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the folding of rocks when plates collided, and they are still rising. The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient block of hard crystalline rock, much older and more stable.
keyPoints: Himalayas: young fold mountains, still rising

How can dams help in controlling floods?
options: They store excess water during heavy rain and release it gradually
They remove all water from rivers

items.q: Name three east-flowing rivers of peninsular India.
items.proposedAnswer: The Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal.

items.q: Why are peninsular rivers less suitable for navigation than the Ganga?
items.proposedAnswer: Peninsular rivers are seasonal and carry little water in dry months, and they flow over uneven plateau land with waterfalls and rapids. This makes boat travel difficult compared with the slow, perennial Ganga on the plains.
keyPoints: Waterfalls and rapids on the plateau
Ganga flows on gentle plains all year

They change the length of the day

options: It is near the equator and has a moderating influence from the surrounding sea
It is surrounded by high mountains

items.q: Why do farmers in Punjab grow wheat in winter rather than in summer?
options: Wheat needs cool weather and gains from winter rain from western disturbances

items.q: Describe two features of the cold weather season in India.
items.proposedAnswer: Temperatures are lowest in the north, with clear skies and cool, dry winds blowing from land to sea. Some winter rain falls in the north-west from western disturbances.
keyPoints: Low temperatures, especially in the north

items.q: Why does rainfall in the Ganga plain generally decrease from east to west?
items.proposedAnswer: The monsoon winds bring moisture from the Bay of Bengal, which is shed as rain as they move inland. By the time they reach the west, such as Delhi, they carry less moisture, so rainfall in Kolkata is greater than in Delhi.
keyPoints: Moisture from the Bay of Bengal
Winds lose moisture as they move inland

What does the term biodiversity mean?
options: The variety of living organisms in an area

items.q: Why is protecting habitats important for saving species?
options: Animals depend on their habitat for food and shelter, so protecting it saves many species together

items.q: What is an endangered species? Name one from India.
items.proposedAnswer: An endangered species is one whose numbers have fallen so low that it is at risk of becoming extinct. The Bengal tiger and the one-horned rhinoceros are examples.
keyPoints: Numbers very low, risk of extinction
Example such as tiger or rhinoceros

items.q: How can local communities help to conserve forests?
items.proposedAnswer: Communities can plant trees, protect forests from illegal cutting and fires, and use forest produce carefully. Working with forest officials, they can guard wildlife and share in the benefits of conservation.

items.q: The number of children born per 1000 persons in a year is called the
What is the Census?
options: A count of the population along with the collection of other data about it

items.q: Why do coastal plains often have a high population?
options: They have ports, fertile land and a moderate climate

items.q: How can better health care affect population growth over time?
options: It always raises the death rate
Death rates fall and growth rises at first, but better health and education can later lower birth rates

items.q: Why is women's education linked with lower birth rates?
options: Educated women are forbidden to marry
Educated women tend to marry later, plan families and have more health knowledge

items.q: What is meant by the occupational structure of a population?
items.proposedAnswer: The occupational structure is the distribution of the working population among different kinds of work, usually grouped into primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
keyPoints: Distribution of workers by type of work

items.q: Suggest two measures to control the rapid growth of population.
items.proposedAnswer: Spreading education, especially among girls and women, and creating awareness about family planning can slow growth. Better health care that lowers infant deaths also encourages smaller families.

items.q: What is a referendum?
options: A direct vote by citizens on a specific question or issue

items.q: In a democracy the majority must also

options: The ruling party postpones elections indefinitely and bans criticism
The press freely reports on the government

items.q: Why does a democracy leave room for correcting mistakes?
options: Citizens can criticise and vote out rulers, so errors become visible and can be changed

items.q: What do we mean by free and fair elections?
items.proposedAnswer: In free and fair elections every adult can vote, parties and candidates are free to compete, voting is secret and results are not rigged or influenced by fear or force.
keyPoints: Secret ballot and no pressure or rigging

items.q: Why is democracy sometimes called government by discussion?
items.proposedAnswer: In a democracy decisions are made after debate and consultation among representatives and citizens, and different views are heard before laws are passed. Discussion helps reach decisions that more people can accept.

items.q: What does equality in the Preamble ensure?

items.q: Which event shows that the Constitution limits the power of the government?
options: A court strikes down a law that violates a Fundamental Right
A new law is passed by Parliament

items.q: What is the difference between the date on which the Indian Constitution was adopted and the date on which it came into force?
items.proposedAnswer: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.

items.q: Why did the framers of the Constitution choose universal adult franchise from the beginning?
items.proposedAnswer: Leaders of the national movement believed in equality, so every adult citizen should have a say in government regardless of wealth, caste or sex. Giving the vote to all gave the new democracy a broad base.

items.q: Where do voters cast their votes on polling day?

options: To let voters choose freely without fear or pressure
To help candidates know who voted for them

items.q: Who is the head of the government in a State?

items.q: What is a party manifesto?
items.proposedAnswer: A manifesto is a document issued by a political party before elections that states its policies and promises to voters about what it will do if it comes to power.
keyPoints: Issued by a party before elections

items.q: Explain why the President is called the nominal head while the Prime Minister is the real executive.
items.proposedAnswer: The President is the formal head of the state, but acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister and the Cabinet take the real decisions and run the government.
keyPoints: Acts on the advice of the ministers
Prime Minister and Cabinet take real decisions

items.q: Which Fundamental Right lets a person take up any profession or occupation?

options: Rights that belong to every person simply because they are human
